name: Hydrogen
notes: Standard atomic weight is the interval [1.00784, 1.00811]; 1.008 is the conventional value (CIAAW).

name: Helium
discoverers: William Ramsay; Per Teodor Cleve and Abraham Langlet
notes: No mp: helium does not solidify at 101.325 kPa (solid helium needs about 2.5 MPa).
Discovered in the solar spectrum in 1868 (Janssen, Lockyer); the year shown is its isolation.

name: Lithium
notes: Standard atomic weight is the interval [6.938, 6.997]; 6.94 is the conventional value (CIAAW).

name: Boron
discoverers: Humphry Davy; Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac and Louis Jacques Thénard
notes: Standard atomic weight is the interval [10.806, 10.821]; 10.81 is the conventional value (CIAAW).

name: Carbon
notes: Standard atomic weight is the interval [12.0096, 12.0116]; 12.011 is the conventional value (CIAAW).
Covalent radius is the mean of Cordero et al.’s sp³, sp² and sp values (76, 73 and 69 pm).
bp is a sublimation point at 1 atm (graphite); it melts only under pressure (triple point 4762 K, 10.3 MPa).

name: Nitrogen
notes: Standard atomic weight is the interval [14.00643, 14.00728]; 14.007 is the conventional value (CIAAW).
Negative electron affinity: the N⁻ anion is unbound.

name: Oxygen
notes: Standard atomic weight is the interval [15.99903, 15.99977]; 15.999 is the conventional value (CIAAW).

name: Magnesium
notes: Standard atomic weight is the interval [24.304, 24.307]; 24.305 is the conventional value (CIAAW).

name: Aluminium
notes: IUPAC name aluminium; US spelling aluminum.

name: Silicon
notes: Standard atomic weight is the interval [28.084, 28.086]; 28.085 is the conventional value (CIAAW).

name: Phosphorus
notes: mp, bp and density are for white phosphorus.

name: Sulfur
notes: Standard atomic weight is the interval [32.059, 32.076]; 32.06 is the conventional value (CIAAW).
mp is for monoclinic sulfur (rhombic S converts to it at 368.35 K); density is for rhombic S.

name: Chlorine
notes: Standard atomic weight is the interval [35.446, 35.457]; 35.45 is the conventional value (CIAAW).

name: Argon
notes: Standard atomic weight is the interval [39.792, 39.963]; 39.95 is the abridged value (CIAAW).

name: Potassium
notes: Density is the X-ray value at 20 °C; the CRC Handbook lists 0.89 g/cm³.

name: Vanadium
notes: Discovered in 1801 by del Río, who withdrew the claim; rediscovered and named by Nils Sefström in 1830.

name: Manganese
notes: Covalent radius is the mean of Cordero et al.’s low- and high-spin values (139 and 161 pm).

name: Iron
notes: Covalent radius is the mean of Cordero et al.’s low- and high-spin values (132 and 152 pm).

name: Cobalt
notes: Covalent radius is the mean of Cordero et al.’s low- and high-spin values (126 and 150 pm).

name: Arsenic
notes: bp is a sublimation point at 1 atm (grey arsenic); it melts only under pressure (triple point 1090 K, 3.7 MPa).

name: Selenium
discoverers: Jöns Jacob Berzelius, Johan Gottlieb Gahn
notes: mp, bp and density are for grey (trigonal) selenium.

name: Bromine
notes: Standard atomic weight is the interval [79.901, 79.907]; 79.904 is the conventional value (CIAAW).

name: Technetium
notes: Mass number: Tc-97 (4.21 Myr) and Tc-98 (4.2 Myr) half-lives overlap within uncertainty; many tables show [98].
Electron affinity is an estimate (±0.2 eV): the Tc⁻ anion has not been measured.
Density is for ⁹⁹Tc metal, the only isotope available in bulk.

name: Tin
notes: mp is for white (β) tin; grey (α) tin converts to white above 286.35 K.

name: Caesium
notes: IUPAC name caesium; US spelling cesium.

name: Cerium
discoverers: Jöns Jacob Berzelius and Wilhelm Hisinger; Martin Heinrich Klaproth

name: Promethium
discoverers: Jacob A. Marinsky, Lawrence E. Glendenin, Charles D. Coryell

name: Dysprosium
notes: Electron affinity omitted: the often-quoted 0.352 eV is not a direct measurement.

name: Ytterbium
notes: Electron affinity is a calculated estimate, not a measurement.

name: Lutetium
notes: Counted as a lanthanide: IUPAC lanthanoids are La-Lu (Red Book 2005, IR-3.5).

name: Tungsten
discoverers: Fausto and Juan José de Elhuyar

name: Rhenium
discoverers: Walter Noddack, Ida Tacke, Otto Berg

name: Iridium
discoverers: Smithson Tennant; Antoine Fourcroy, Louis-Nicolas Vauquelin, Hippolyte-Victor Collet-Descotils

name: Thallium
notes: Standard atomic weight is the interval [204.382, 204.385]; 204.38 is the conventional value (CIAAW).

name: Lead
notes: Standard atomic weight is the interval [206.14, 207.94]; 207.2 is the abridged value (CIAAW).

name: Bismuth
notes: ²⁰⁹Bi is alpha-radioactive (half-life about 2×10¹⁹ years; de Marcillac et al. 2003) but is treated as stable.

name: Polonium
notes: Classed as a post-transition metal (a metallic solid); some tables list it as a metalloid.
Electron affinity has not been measured.
Occurs naturally as a U/Th decay-series member; no Goldschmidt class assigned.

name: Astatine
discoverers: Dale R. Corson, Kenneth R. MacKenzie, Emilio Segrè
notes: Class contested: tracer chemistry shows both halide-like At⁻ and cationic At⁺; bulk At has never been made and is predicted to be metallic (Hermann et al. 2013).
Never isolated in bulk: mp, density and phase are estimates.
Occurs naturally as a U/Th decay-series member; no Goldschmidt class assigned.

name: Radon
notes: Discovered as thorium emanation (1899); Friedrich Dorn’s 1900 radium emanation is often cited instead.
Occurs naturally as a U/Th decay-series member; no Goldschmidt class assigned.

name: Francium
notes: Never isolated in bulk: mp is an estimate near room temperature, so the phase is unknown.
Occurs naturally as a U/Th decay-series member; no Goldschmidt class assigned.

name: Radium
discoverers: Pierre Curie, Marie Curie, Gustave Bémont
notes: Density is the X-ray value from the bcc lattice (a = 514.8 pm).

name: Actinium
notes: Discovery credit is disputed: Debierne’s 1899 samples are questioned, and Friedrich Giesel isolated actinium independently in 1902.
Occurs naturally as a U/Th decay-series member; no Goldschmidt class assigned.

name: Protactinium
notes: Discovered as ²³⁴ᵐPa (1913); long-lived ²³¹Pa was found in 1917-18 by Hahn and Meitner and by Soddy and Cranston.

name: Neptunium
discoverers: Edwin M. McMillan, Philip H. Abelson

name: Plutonium
discoverers: Glenn T. Seaborg, Edwin M. McMillan, Joseph W. Kennedy, Arthur C. Wahl

name: Americium
discoverers: Glenn T. Seaborg, Ralph A. James, Leon O. Morgan, Albert Ghiorso
notes: Density is the X-ray value for dhcp ²⁴¹Am; the CRC Handbook lists 12 g/cm³.

name: Curium
discoverers: Glenn T. Seaborg, Ralph A. James, Albert Ghiorso

name: Berkelium
discoverers: Stanley G. Thompson, Albert Ghiorso, Glenn T. Seaborg

name: Californium
discoverers: Stanley G. Thompson, Kenneth Street Jr., Albert Ghiorso, Glenn T. Seaborg

name: Einsteinium
discoverers: Albert Ghiorso et al. (Berkeley, Argonne, Los Alamos)
notes: Density is the X-ray value for fcc ²⁵³Es metal (a = 575 pm; Haire & Baybarz 1979).

name: Fermium
discoverers: Albert Ghiorso et al. (Berkeley, Argonne, Los Alamos)
notes: Surface-ionization measurement gives IE1 = 6.52 ± 0.13 eV (Sato et al. 2018), consistent with this value.

name: Mendelevium
discoverers: Albert Ghiorso, Bernard G. Harvey, Gregory R. Choppin, Stanley G. Thompson, Glenn T. Seaborg
notes: Surface-ionization measurement gives IE1 = 6.59 ± 0.13 eV (Sato et al. 2018), consistent with this value.

name: Nobelium
discoverers: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research, Dubna
notes: Oxidation state +2 is the most stable in water, unusual among actinides.
A 1957 Stockholm discovery claim was not confirmed; IUPAC/IUPAP credited Dubna (1966).

name: Lawrencium
discoverers: Albert Ghiorso, Torbjørn Sikkeland, Almon E. Larsh, Robert M. Latimer
notes: Counted as an actinide: IUPAC actinoids are Ac-Lr (Red Book 2005, IR-3.5).
The 7p1 configuration is predicted; the measured ionization energy (Sato et al. 2015) supports it.
IUPAC/IUPAP (1993) shared the discovery credit between Berkeley and Dubna.

name: Rutherfordium
notes: IUPAC/IUPAP (1993) shared the discovery credit between Berkeley and Dubna.
Made only a few atoms at a time: bulk properties such as density are unknown.

name: Dubnium
notes: Oxidation state +5 is established with single atoms, in volatile DbOCl₃ (Chiera et al. 2021).
IUPAC/IUPAP (1993) shared the discovery credit between Berkeley and Dubna.
Made only a few atoms at a time: bulk properties such as density are unknown.

name: Seaborgium
discoverers: Albert Ghiorso et al. (Berkeley and Livermore)
notes: Oxidation state +6 is established with single atoms, in volatile SgO₂Cl₂ (Schädel et al. 1997).
Made only a few atoms at a time: bulk properties such as density are unknown.

name: Bohrium
notes: Oxidation state +7 is established with single atoms, in volatile BhO₃Cl (Eichler et al. 2000).
Made only a few atoms at a time: bulk properties such as density are unknown.

name: Hassium
notes: Mass number: Hs-269 (15 s) and Hs-270 (9 s) half-lives overlap within uncertainty (NUBASE2020).
Oxidation state +8 is established with single atoms, in volatile HsO₄ (Düllmann et al. 2002).
Made only a few atoms at a time: bulk properties such as density are unknown.

name: Meitnerium
notes: Mass number: Mt-277 (9 s) and Mt-278 (6 s) half-lives overlap within uncertainty (NUBASE2020).
Made only a few atoms at a time: bulk properties such as density are unknown.

name: Darmstadtium
notes: Configuration from relativistic calculations (6d8 7s2), not the 6d9 7s1 Pt analogy.
Made only a few atoms at a time: bulk properties such as density are unknown.

name: Roentgenium
notes: Configuration from relativistic calculations (6d9 7s2), not the 6d10 7s1 Au analogy.
Made only a few atoms at a time: bulk properties such as density are unknown.

name: Copernicium
notes: Made only a few atoms at a time: bulk properties such as density are unknown.

name: Nihonium
notes: First atom made in 2004; IUPAC/IUPAP credited the discovery in 2015.
Made only a few atoms at a time: bulk properties such as density are unknown.

name: Flerovium
discoverers: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory
notes: Made only a few atoms at a time: bulk properties such as density are unknown.

name: Moscovium
discoverers: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research, Lawrence Livermore and Oak Ridge National Laboratories
notes: First atoms made in 2003 by Dubna and Livermore; IUPAC/IUPAP (2015) credited the discovery to Dubna, Livermore and Oak Ridge for experiments from 2010 on.
Made only a few atoms at a time: bulk properties such as density are unknown.

name: Livermorium
discoverers: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory
notes: Made only a few atoms at a time: bulk properties such as density are unknown.

name: Tennessine
discoverers: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research, Lawrence Livermore and Oak Ridge National Laboratories
notes: Class predicted: Ts has never been studied chemically; relativistic effects and the rise in metallic character down group 17 point to a metal rather than a halogen-like nonmetal.
Made only a few atoms at a time: bulk properties such as density are unknown.

name: Oganesson
discoverers: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory
notes: Group 18, but predicted to be a semiconducting solid at room temperature (Smits et al. 2020).
Made only a few atoms at a time: bulk properties such as density are unknown.
